title: [CQ-C02b1] Daemon snapshot manifest verification
description:
Objective: give the daemon its own pure verifier for R09's frozen SourceSnapshot. The snapshot is the {version:1, commit, tree, base, overlay, excluded} object that scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs exportSourceSnapshot resolves. Both base and overlay are validateImport results ({entries, digest}) from scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs. The CQ-C02b snapshot source adapter (task-311dbda4) then serves context only from bytes the daemon itself re-verified, never from writer declarations.

Split out of CQ-C02b by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-29. The reason is size: verification plus serving, with tests, is about 420 lines, over QA's 400 net cap. Verification is the self-contained, security-relevant seam, as R09a was for R09.

Interface (CQ-C02b plans against these exact names):
- New module packages/moe-daemon/src/context/snapshotManifest.ts.
- `export type SnapshotRefusal = 'SNAPSHOT_INPUT_INVALID' | 'SNAPSHOT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED' | 'SNAPSHOT_ENTRY_INVALID' | 'SNAPSHOT_SYMLINK_DENIED' | 'SNAPSHOT_PATH_INVALID' | 'SNAPSHOT_CONTROL_PATH' | 'SNAPSHOT_PATH_COLLISION' | 'SNAPSHOT_HASH_MISMATCH' | 'SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_MISMATCH'`.
- `export interface VerifiedSnapshotFile { readonly path: string; readonly executable: boolean; readonly size: number; readonly sha256: string; readonly data: Uint8Array }`. data is a private copy; sha256 is recomputed from that copy.
- `export interface VerifiedSnapshot { readonly version: 1; readonly commit: string; readonly tree: string; readonly identity: { readonly base: string; readonly overlay: string }; readonly base: ReadonlyMap<string, VerifiedSnapshotFile>; readonly overlay: ReadonlyMap<string, VerifiedSnapshotFile | { readonly kind: 'delete'; readonly path: string }>; readonly excluded: number }`. The identity digests are recomputed with R09a's framing.
- `export function verifySourceSnapshot(raw: unknown): { ok: true; snapshot: VerifiedSnapshot } | { ok: false; code: SnapshotRefusal; layer?: 'base' | 'overlay' }`. It is pure: no filesystem, process, network or Git access. It never throws, and it never returns a partial view.
- `export function snapshotPathRefusal(path: string): 'SNAPSHOT_PATH_INVALID' | 'SNAPSHOT_CONTROL_PATH' | null`. This is R09a's validateImportPath ported verbatim to TypeScript: the CONTROL_SEGMENTS list at any depth after foldCase, FORBIDDEN_CHAR, DEVICE_NAME, 8.3 short names, NFC and well-formedness, and the 1024-byte path and 255-byte segment bounds. A control segment is checked before portability.

Rules:
- Exact keys and plain prototypes. data is a Uint8Array or Buffer measured with the intrinsic byteLength getter, then copied before it is hashed.
- size must equal the byte length. A declared sha256 that differs from the recomputed one gives SNAPSHOT_HASH_MISMATCH. A declared layer digest that differs from the recomputed one gives SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_MISMATCH.
- Entries are sorted by UTF-8 path bytes and unique.
- Collisions are refused within a layer, as in R09a's refuseCollisions, and across the merged view: a base file that is an ancestor of an overlay file not deleted by the overlay.
- Base holds file entries only.
- R09a's bounds apply: 10,000 entries and 256 MiB.
- version is 1. commit and tree are full lowercase ids. excluded is a non-negative safe integer.

Scope boundaries: verification and its regression tests only. No serving, no activation, no MCP tool, no scripts/ change. Consume the LANDED R09a and R09b format; do not redefine it. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout (2026-10-24). Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Never directly edit .moe.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: verifySourceSnapshot accepts exactly the frozen SourceSnapshot that R09b exportSourceSnapshot resolves, and returns a frozen view whose identity digests and per-file sha256 are recomputed from the entry bytes. A conformance test feeds the same entries through the landed scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs validateImport and asserts equal digests and sha256 values. The test is skipped only when scripts/ is absent, as in the Docker context.

snapshotPathRefusal matches R09a validateImportPath on a shared table: control segments at any depth and case-folded, traversal, empty and dot segments, forbidden and invisible characters, device and 8.3 short names, non-NFC text, and the byte bounds. Every row gives the same accept/refuse outcome and code through both implementations.

A malformed, symlink, colliding (within a layer or across the merged view), out-of-bounds, sha256-mismatched or digest-mismatched input returns { ok: false, code } with one fixed SnapshotRefusal, never a partial view and never a throw. Hostile shapes (exotic prototypes, accessors, Proxies, spoofed byteLength) are covered, and each code has a named test that fails when its guard is removed.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0, and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Port R09a's path rule.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/context/snapshotManifest.ts. It is PURE: it imports only node:crypto, and the source is ASCII-only.
- Header comment: the module mirrors scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs (R09a) validateImportPath and seal framing, so keep the two in sync. A parity test pins them.
- Constants, all exported:
  - SNAPSHOT_MAX_PATH_BYTES 1024, SNAPSHOT_MAX_SEGMENT_BYTES 255, SNAPSHOT_MAX_ENTRIES 10000, SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES 268435456.
  - SNAPSHOT_CONTROL_SEGMENTS: the frozen list '.git', '.gitmodules', '.moe', '.mcp.json', '.claude', '.codex', '.gemini', '.grok', '.worktrees'.
- Private regexes:
  - FORBIDDEN_CHAR, byte-identical to R09a's: backslash, colon, Windows-reserved, C0/DEL/C1, U+061C, U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060-U+206F and U+FEFF, all written as escapes.
  - DEVICE_NAME, with the superscripts escaped as ¹, ² and ³.
- Private helpers: foldCase (upper-then-lower), isShortName (8.3 shape), portableSegment, wellFormed and utf8Length.

`export function snapshotPathRefusal(path: string): 'SNAPSHOT_PATH_INVALID' | 'SNAPSHOT_CONTROL_PATH' | null` follows R09a's order exactly:
1. A non-string, empty or over-bound path gives INVALID.
2. Any segment that is a control segment after foldCase gives CONTROL. This check runs BEFORE portability, so '.git/CON' is CONTROL.
3. Then: not well-formed, not NFC, FORBIDDEN_CHAR, or a non-portable segment (empty, '.', '..', over 255 bytes, a leading space, a trailing space or dot, a device name, an 8.3 short name) gives INVALID.
4. Otherwise null.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/context/snapshotManifest.test.ts with test P1, a shared path table of [path, expected code or null]. Rows:
- portable paths: 'a.ts', 'src/x/y.md', NFC 'é.ts', 'a.b.c';
- control at any depth and case: '.git', '.git/x', 'a/.GIT/x', '.moe/p.json', 'x/.Moe', '.mcp.json', '.claude/x', '.codex', '.gemini/x', '.grok', '.worktrees/a', '.gitmodules', dotless-i '.gıt', and '.git/CON' (CONTROL wins);
- traversal and empty: '..', 'a/../b', './a', 'a/./b', 'a//b', '/a', 'a/';
- forbidden characters: backslash, ':', '<', NUL, U+202E, U+FEFF, U+200B, U+061C, U+009F;
- device names: 'CON', 'con.txt', 'a/NUL', 'COM1', 'LPT¹', 'CON .txt', 'CONIN$';
- 8.3 short names: 'PROGRA~1', 'GIT~1', 'a/ABCDEFGH~12.txt';
- trailing and leading spaces or dots: 'a.', 'a ', ' a';
- non-NFC 'é.ts' and a lone surrogate;
- bounds: a 1024-byte path is ok, 1025 bytes is INVALID; a 255-byte segment is ok, 256 bytes is INVALID.

Assert every row through snapshotPathRefusal. When the repo's scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs exists (resolve the repo root relatively from import.meta.url and load it with a dynamic import of pathToFileURL(...).href), also run each row through R09a validateImportPath: a throw maps to its error.code, a return maps to null. Assert identical outcomes and codes. Use describe/it.skipIf when scripts/ is absent, as in the Docker context.

To write the \u escapes, follow mem gotcha-js-hostile-input-species-and-literal-escapes, then check that `LC_ALL=C grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7f]'` finds nothing in either file.
implementationPlan.note: snapshotPathRefusal ported from R09a validateImportPath; FORBIDDEN_CHAR/DEVICE_NAME lines copied byte-for-byte from source-snapshot.mjs (the Write tool decoded \u escapes into literal chars on first write, so I replaced the lines from R09a by script; both files are ASCII-only, checked with LC_ALL=C grep -P). P1: 58 table rows plus the R09a parity row, 59/59 green in a Linux snapshot (vitest, node v24.21.0). Plan deviation: the plan's row 'a/ABCDEFGH~12.txt' is NOT an 8.3 name (its base is 11 chars), so it is listed as accepted as 'ABCDEFGH~12.txt', and 'a/ABCDE~12.txt' is the refused short-name row. I added a multibyte segment-bound pair (127x U+00E9 + 'a' ok, 128x U+00E9 INVALID) and a non-string row (42). Shared checkout has ~625 peers' dirty paths; I left them untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement `export function verifySourceSnapshot(raw: unknown)` in snapshotManifest.ts. Export the SnapshotRefusal, VerifiedSnapshotFile and VerifiedSnapshot types exactly as task-02fd5931's description names them; CQ-C02b (task-311dbda4) plans against those names.

Never throws, and never returns a partial view (mem gotcha-pure-validator-hostile-input):
- Wrap ALL reads in one try/catch. An unexpected throw from a getter, Proxy trap or revoked proxy maps to SNAPSHOT_INPUT_INVALID at the top level and SNAPSHOT_ENTRY_INVALID inside an entry.
- Read every property once into a local.
- Check own keys with Reflect.ownKeys for an exact match.
- Accept only plain prototypes: Object.prototype or null.

Snapshot level:
- Exact keys {version, commit, tree, base, overlay, excluded}.
- version === 1.
- commit and tree are full lowercase hex ids of the same length (40 or 64), checked with typeof === 'string' plus /^[0-9a-f]{40}$|^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ with no m flag.
- excluded is a non-negative safe integer.
- Each layer has exact keys {entries, digest}. digest is 64-char lowercase hex.
- entries is a real Array with prototype Array.prototype. Read its length ONCE and require Number.isInteger && >= 0 && <= SNAPSHOT_MAX_ENTRIES. Over the cap gives LIMIT_EXCEEDED, any other failure INPUT_INVALID. Then loop index < count reading entries[index] once each: no slice, map or species copy.

Entries:
- kind 'symlink' gives SNAPSHOT_SYMLINK_DENIED, checked first, as R09a does.
- File keys are exactly {kind, path, executable, size, sha256, data}: the SEALED shape R09a's seal returns and R09b's layers carry. Delete keys are exactly {kind, path}. Anything else gives ENTRY_INVALID.
- path goes through snapshotPathRefusal; its code is returned as is.
- executable is boolean.
- data is an ArrayBuffer view whose prototype is Uint8Array.prototype or Buffer.prototype.
- size is the intrinsic byteLength, read through the %TypedArray%.prototype getter captured at module load. The declared size must be a safe integer equal to it, else ENTRY_INVALID.
- Running total > SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES gives LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Check it BEFORE copying or hashing.
- Copy with new Uint8Array(data) and require copy.byteLength === size.
- The declared sha256 must be 64-char lowercase hex, else ENTRY_INVALID. If it differs from sha256(copy), give SNAPSHOT_HASH_MISMATCH.
- Base must hold files only; a delete there gives ENTRY_INVALID.
- Entries must be strictly increasing by Buffer.compare of their UTF-8 path bytes. An exact repeat gives PATH_COLLISION; any other order gives ENTRY_INVALID.
- Within a layer, a case-folded duplicate or an ancestor/descendant pair gives SNAPSHOT_PATH_COLLISION, through R09a's folded-segment trie.
- An overlay delete must name an existing base file, as R09b only ever emits; otherwise ENTRY_INVALID.

Layer digest:
- Recompute it with R09a's framing:
  1. 'moe-source-snapshot-v1\0';
  2. u32be(count);
  3. per entry in path-byte order: the kind byte (0x46 file, 0x44 delete), u32be(path byte length) and the path bytes;
  4. a file adds the executable byte, u32be(size) and the 32 raw sha256 bytes.
- A recomputed digest that differs from the declared one gives SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_MISMATCH, with the layer named.

Merged view:
- base files, minus overlay deletes, plus overlay files (an overlay file replaces a base file at the same path).
- Run the same trie over it. Any case-folded duplicate or ancestor pair across layers gives SNAPSHOT_PATH_COLLISION. Examples: base file 'x' plus overlay file 'x/y' with no delete of 'x'; base 'A.ts' plus overlay 'a.ts'.

Result:
- Return {ok:true, snapshot}: a frozen object with frozen identity {base, overlay} = the recomputed digests, and Maps of frozen VerifiedSnapshotFile {path, executable, size, sha256, data: the private copy} plus frozen {kind:'delete', path}.
- Every failure returns {ok:false, code, layer?}.

Tests, in the same file, table-driven:
- V1 conformance (skipIf no scripts/): build base and overlay with R09a validateImport, assemble the snapshot, and verify. Assert ok; identity equal to each digest; per-file sha256 equal; Object.isFrozen on the view, identity and entries; and that mutating the input data after verification leaves view.data unchanged.
- V3 refusals: ONE named row per code. Each mutates a structuredClone of a good snapshot.
  - INPUT_INVALID: null, an array, a missing key, an extra key, version 2, an uppercase commit, a 40/64 length mismatch, excluded -1, 1.5 and '0', and a class-instance prototype.
  - LIMIT_EXCEEDED: a length of 10001, and one zero-filled Uint8Array of 2**28+1 bytes (refused before hashing).
  - ENTRY_INVALID: missing size, an extra key, a size mismatch, a non-boolean executable, a number-array data, a Float64Array, an uppercase sha256, a delete in base, an orphan overlay delete, unsorted entries, and an own byteLength spoof.
  - SYMLINK_DENIED: in either layer.
  - PATH_INVALID and CONTROL_PATH: entry paths.
  - PATH_COLLISION: a repeat, a case-fold, an ancestor, and the 3 cross-layer cases.
  - HASH_MISMATCH: flip a byte, keep the declared sha256.
  - DIGEST_MISMATCH: a wrong digest, or a flipped executable bit with the digest kept.
- V4 hostile: a Symbol, a BigInt, a function, Proxies with throwing get, ownKeys and getPrototypeOf traps, a revoked Proxy, and a counting getter (read exactly once). Each gives ok:false with no throw.
- V5: an entries array with its own constructor[Symbol.species], and a Proxy over an array whose length is an object, give INPUT_INVALID or no effect, and the count is read once.

Error handling: every branch returns a code. Never rethrow.
implementationPlan.note: verifySourceSnapshot implemented with the exact exported names (SnapshotRefusal, VerifiedSnapshotFile, VerifiedSnapshot), plus an exported alias SnapshotVerification for the result union. Refusals are module-minted objects tracked in a WeakSet (not instanceof), so a thrown hostile Proxy can neither pose as one nor throw again from the catch. Layer-scoped refusals carry layer:'base'|'overlay'; top-level and merged-view refusals carry none. Byte bound is per layer (256 MiB each), as R09b bounds each validateImport separately; a combined bound would refuse legitimate exports. Tests: a test-side seal() oracle (independent framing) builds fixtures, so V3-V5 run without scripts/; V1 checks the oracle and the verifier against R09a validateImport. V3 has 39 named rows covering all 9 codes, including a trailing-newline digest (m-flag), a proto-swapped Float64Array (reaches the copy-length guard QA flagged as untested in R09a), and 3 cross-layer collisions asserted with no layer. V4: null/array/Symbol/BigInt/function, get/ownKeys/getPrototypeOf trap Proxies, a revoked Proxy, a throwing entry Proxy, a thrown hostile Proxy, and once-only getters on 14 properties. V5: own species constructor never invoked; Proxy length read once; an object length is never coerced. 112/112 green in the Linux snapshot; tsc --noEmit clean. Plan deviation: the V4 counting-getter row expects ok:true with every count 1 (the getters return undefined after the first read), not ok:false. Size so far 218 + 158 = 376 lines.

implementationPlan.description:
Add the real-producer conformance test and the purity test to snapshotManifest.test.ts. Both are skipped only when scripts/ is absent.

V2:
1. In a mkdtemp git repo (follow repositorySource.test.ts's temp-repo pattern: execFileSync git with a GIT_*-scrubbed env, cleaned in afterAll), commit 'a.ts' and 'dir/b.ts'.
2. Modify 'a.ts', delete 'dir/b.ts', and add an untracked 'c.ts' plus '.moe/x.json'.
3. Run the LANDED scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs exportSourceSnapshot({repoDir, commit}).
4. Assert:
- verifySourceSnapshot(export) is ok, and its identity equals {base: export.base.digest, overlay: export.overlay.digest}.
- The overlay map holds a.ts and c.ts as files and dir/b.ts as a delete.
- excluded equals the export's excluded, and '.moe/x.json' is in neither map.
- A structuredClone of the export that gains an extra key is refused INPUT_INVALID. That proves exact keys hold against the real shape.
Error handling: an export failure fails the test with its error code; never skip on a failure.

V6: read snapshotManifest.ts as text and assert:
- it is ASCII-only (no char above 0x7f, which also rules out Trojan Source);
- it imports only 'node:crypto';
- it contains no fs, child_process or process.env.

It runs the LANDED exportSourceSnapshot; an export failure fails the test with its code. Asserts: ok; identity equals both export digests; base keys [a.ts, dir/b.ts]; overlay [a.ts file, c.ts file, dir/b.ts delete]; excluded 1 on both sides, so .moe/x.json is in neither map; a structuredClone plus an extra key is INPUT_INVALID. V6: the module's only import is node:crypto; no fs, child_process, process.env, import( or require(; both files have no char above 0x7f. V6 runs unconditionally (it needs no scripts/), which is stricter than the plan's skipIf. 114/114 green, tsc clean. I trimmed the module (a header line, a loop, a comment) to keep the total at 398 lines (module 213 + test 185). Fixed one bug in my own draft: a mkdirSync(...) ?? writeFileSync helper skipped the write, because mkdirSync returns a path.

Mutation sweep: /tmp/moe-c02b1-mut/mutate.mjs ran each mutant against the snapshot copy only. 52 mutants, 48 killed.
Plan list, all killed: control-after-portability (P1 '.git/CON'), isShortName (P1), lower-only fold (P1 '.gıt'), symlink check (V3), size===byteLength (V3), view data = input (V1), sha256 compare (V3 HASH), digest compare (V3 DIGEST x3), cross-layer trie (3 cross rows), re-read length (V5), entry catch and top-level catch (V4).
Also killed: wellFormed, NFC, path and segment utf8 bounds, HEX64 m flag, FULL_ID m flag, typeof commit/tree, version, excluded integer/sign, byte and entry LIMIT, count-integer guard, copy-length guard, view-prototype check, delete-names-base, order check, plain prototype, key count, Array.isArray-only, Array.prototype-only, typeof executable, sha256 and digest formats, kind and executable digest bytes, freeze, all 3 trie guards, control fold, and owned() reading a prototype.
Rows added this step to kill survivors (all inline): multibyte path over 1024 bytes; Uint8ClampedArray; String commit/tree; ids with a trailing newline; subclassed entries; array-like entries.
4 equivalent survivors:
(1) the path.length precheck, since utf8 length >= .length;
(2) hashing the input instead of the copy, since no input code runs between copy and hash, and V1 kills the view-is-input variant;
(3) the exact-repeat check, since the trie gives the same PATH_COLLISION;
(4) data.byteLength instead of the intrinsic getter, since the copy-length guard gives the same ENTRY_INVALID; only the pre-copy memory bound differs.
Size: 213 + 186 = 399 lines, both new files, under 400.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of this task's own two files. A RESUME session re-verified the state from disk: both files matched checkpoint 34a440c before this step's edits.

Can any input throw, return ok with unhashed bytes, or hash something other than what was validated? No. I probed this with a scratch script against the real module:
- A DataView, a BigInt64Array posing as a Uint8Array, a detached view (size 0) and a getter throwing a primitive string all give ENTRY_INVALID with no throw.
- A resizable length-tracking view and a SharedArrayBuffer view verify correctly, and the copy is a private, non-shared buffer.
- Proxies, accessors, species and a spoofed byteLength are already covered by V3/V4/V5.
- Each property is read once. viewLength runs the intrinsic getter, the copy follows with no input code in between, and only the copy is hashed.

O(n^2)? None:
- the trie is linear in total path length;
- key and prototype checks run on constant-size lists;
- path.length is bounded before the UTF-8 measurement.

Parity with R09a:
- snapshotPathRefusal, FORBIDDEN_CHAR, DEVICE_NAME, foldCase, isShortName, portableSegment, the trie and the digest framing match source-snapshot.mjs line by line;
- the P1 parity row, V1 and V2 are green.

Purity: imports only node:crypto. Both files are ASCII-only with no CR, and contain no forbidden token (grep exit 1).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Import scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs from the daemon at runtime. Rejected: the daemon is a separate package; the IDE bundles and the Docker image ship packages/moe-daemon alone. So the daemon gets a verbatim TypeScript port, pinned by a parity table and conformance tests against the landed module.
2. Re-run R09a's validateImport on the sealed layers. Rejected: validateImport takes UNSEALED input entries {kind, path, executable, data} and recomputes everything, but the R09b SourceSnapshot carries SEALED entries {kind, path, executable, size, sha256, data}. The daemon must verify the sealed shape and compare the declarations against recomputation (HASH/DIGEST mismatch codes).
3. Throw fixed-code errors as R09a does. Rejected for the daemon API: a discriminated {ok, code} result keeps the CQ-C02b adapter's 'snapshot-unverifiable:<code>' mapping exception-free.
4. Reuse workloadSnapshot.ts checkPortablePath. Rejected: it is not exported, not equal to R09a (no control segments, only the .git and git~1 short names), and it throws invalidInput with path text.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Landed facts from R09a source-snapshot.mjs:
- seal() returns Object.freeze({entries: frozen sorted entries, digest}). File entries are {kind, path, executable, size, sha256 hex, data}; deletes are {kind, path}.
- The digest framing is the one in step 2.
- CONTROL_SEGMENTS are refused at any depth after foldCase, and BEFORE portability.
- validateImport refuses symlink kinds first and measures data with the intrinsic byteLength getter.
- Its QA (round 2) required: read the count once, no species copies, an ASCII-only source.

Landed facts from R09b source-export.mjs:
- exportSourceSnapshot resolves Object.freeze({version:1, commit, tree, base, overlay, excluded}).
- The overlay holds only changed files and deletes of committed paths. Control paths are excluded and counted.
- A file-to-directory replacement collides inside validateImport.

Daemon tests may import scripts/*.mjs through a repo-relative file URL, skipped when absent (the Docker context). Daemon tests run only in a Linux-native snapshot from WSL.
planningNotes.risks:
- Port drift from R09a: the P1 parity table plus V1/V2 conformance catch it while scripts/ exists.
- Hostile-input escapes:
  - wrap every read;
  - read the count once, and loop only by index;
  - use the intrinsic byteLength getter;
  - hash the private copy only.
- 256 MiB allocation in tests: use one zero-filled 2**28+1 buffer, which is lazily committed, and refuse it before any copy or hash.
- Size: about 150 runtime plus 210 test lines, so stay table-driven to remain under 400 net.
- Rails:
  - Never spell the forbidden dunder-prototype token, even in a test; use Object.create(null) or Object.setPrototypeOf.
  - No .moe edits and no Git writes; temp repos only.
- Interface: the exact names are a contract for CQ-C02b (task-311dbda4, already planned against them). Renaming one requires amending that plan.
